topics.title: Intended purpose and affected decisions
topics.hint: intended purpose use for which an AI system is intended
topics.default_q: Could you briefly describe what the agent we will assess does?

topics.title: EU link
topics.hint: scope applies to providers deployers located in the Union output used in the Union
topics.default_q: Is the agent used in the EU, or do its outputs affect people or organisations in the EU?
options: Yes, it is used in the EU
topics.simple_q: In short: do people living in the EU, or an organisation in the EU, use the agent's outputs or get affected by them? If you are unsure, you can list the countries of your customers and your organisation.

topics.title: Role of the organisation
topics.hint: provider deployer importer distributor definitions role
topics.default_q: Did your organisation build this agent, or does it use an agent that someone else built?

topics.title: Usage status and date
topics.hint: date of application obligations apply from
topics.default_q: Is the agent live now, or is this a planned use?

topics.title: Standard prohibited-use check
topics.hint: prohibited artificial intelligence practices biometric emotion manipulative techniques social scoring risk assessment natural persons
topics.default_q: Standard check, asked for every agent: does your agent do any of the following? Tick everything that applies, or choose “None of these”. Anything you already told me is left out. You can also describe it in your own words.
topics.simple_q: In short, do any of these apply? For example: face recognition at a door or emotion analysis from a camera; messages written to persuade someone to buy something or change their mind; or a score or ranking number given to applicants, customers or employees. Tick what applies, or say you are not sure.

items.label: It uses biometric data (face, voice, fingerprints) to recognise people or work out something about them, such as emotions
It is meant to steer the people it deals with towards a behaviour, such as buying, clicking, voting or giving up (a plain recommendation to a decision maker does not count)
It gives people a score, a rank or a risk/suitability value

multi.unsure_label: I'm not sure about some of these

topics.title: Biometrics screening
topics.hint: prohibited biometric categorisation emotion inference facial images remote biometric identification
topics.default_q: Does the agent use biometric data such as face, voice or fingerprints to recognise people or infer their characteristics?
topics.simple_q: For example: face recognition at a door, voice-based identity verification, fingerprint reading, or emotion analysis from a camera. Is there anything like that?

topics.title: Behaviour steering screening
topics.hint: prohibited manipulative deceptive techniques exploit vulnerabilities distort behaviour
topics.default_q: Is the agent's purpose to steer the people it meets towards a specific behaviour (buying, clicking, voting, giving up)? Merely giving a recommendation to a decision maker does not count.
topics.simple_q: For example: does it generate messages designed to persuade a user to buy something or change their mind?

topics.title: Scoring of people screening
topics.hint: prohibited social scoring risk assessment of natural persons criminal offence profiling
topics.default_q: Does the agent assign people a score, a rank or a risk/suitability value?
topics.simple_q: For example: does it give applicants, customers or employees a score or a ranking number?

topics.title: Conditions and exceptions of a possible prohibition
topics.hint: prohibited practices conditions exceptions
topics.default_q: I need to clarify which feature in the prohibited-use screening applies.

topics.title: Sensitive use area
topics.hint: high-risk AI systems Annex III areas employment education essential services law enforcement migration justice biometrics
topics.default_q: Does the agent's task fall into one of these areas: recruitment/employee management, education/exams, access to essential services such as credit, insurance or social benefits, law enforcement, migration/borders, justice/elections, or critical infrastructure?
topics.simple_q: For example: is it used in a decision process that affects a person's life, such as recruitment, a credit or insurance application, school/exams, police or migration procedures?

topics.title: Profiling
topics.hint: profiling of natural persons always high-risk Annex III
topics.default_q: In this task, does the agent evaluate people and build profiles of them?
topics.simple_q: Does the agent automatically assess a person's personality, behaviour or interests and build a profile?

topics.title: Product safety component
topics.hint: safety component of a product Union harmonisation legislation third-party conformity assessment Article 6(1) needs both conditions
topics.default_q: Is the agent a safety component of a regulated product (such as a medical device, machinery or a toy), or the product itself? If so, must that product pass an independent safety check by an outside body (a notified body) before it is sold?
options: Yes, and the product must pass an independent safety check by an outside body (a notified body) before it is sold
Yes, but the product does not need an independent safety check by an outside body
Yes, but I don't know whether an independent safety check is needed
No, it is not part of a regulated product

topics.title: Tool and action inventory
topics.hint: tool access permissions actions
topics.default_q: Which tools, systems, accounts and data sources can the agent access, and for each one what can it do (read, write, modify, delete, send, execute or transact)?
options: Can also change or send information
topics.simple_q: For example, can it only read CVs from a database, or can it also change candidate records, send messages or reject applications?

topics.title: Action authority
topics.hint: agent tools access permissions actions autonomy latitude
topics.default_q: What can the agent do on its own, and does a person have to approve it first? Please describe each kind of action, for example: “it answers customers by itself, but refunds need an employee’s approval”.
options: Prepares drafts, a human sends them
topics.simple_q: For example: can the agent send an e-mail, make a payment or change a record on its own, or does it only prepare a recommendation for a person?

topics.title: Review of the recommendation
topics.hint: human oversight reviewers understand outputs automation bias ability to override
topics.default_q: Can the employee who decides see what information the agent's recommendation is based on?
options: Yes, they can see the basis
No, they only see the result

topics.title: Is there human approval
topics.hint: human approval before actions oversight intervention
topics.default_q: Before the agent carries out an action, does a person have to approve it? If it depends on the amount or the kind of action, please describe the rule.
topics.simple_q: For example: before a payment, sending an e-mail or changing a record, does someone press an 'approve' button?

topics.title: Action-specific approval
topics.hint: human approval before actions bound to the specific action oversight intervention
topics.default_q: Is this approval specific to that single action (details such as amount and recipient approved one by one), or is it a general/bulk approval?
topics.simple_q: For example: does the approver see and approve the amount and recipient each time, or was a one-time general permission given?

topics.title: Enforcement of limits
topics.hint: permission limits allowlist enforced technically tools scope budget caps
topics.default_q: Are the agent’s limits (for example the maximum amount, or which systems it can reach) enforced by the system itself, or only written down in instructions?
topics.simple_q: For example: is the maximum amount blocked by code in the system, or is there only an instruction telling the agent 'do not exceed this much'?

topics.title: Authority expansion
topics.hint: authority expansion privilege escalation delegation ceiling dynamic permissions
topics.default_q: Can the agent give itself more permissions or access on its own while it is working?
topics.simple_q: For example: can the agent add a new tool, permission or access for itself for its task?

topics.title: Delegation to other agents
topics.hint: multi-agent delegation orchestrator subagents accountability
topics.default_q: Does the agent delegate part of its work to other agents or automated tools?

topics.title: Reasonable worst-case harm
topics.hint: risk of harm to health safety fundamental rights severity of harm
topics.default_q: What is the worst reasonable outcome if the agent makes a mistake (financial loss, privacy breach, loss of rights, safety)? For employment decisions, could qualified candidates lose a job opportunity?
topics.simple_q: If the agent recommends or does something wrong, what would be the worst outcome: a small correction, a financial loss, a serious loss of rights? Losing a job opportunity can be serious even if a person decides.

topics.title: Reversibility
topics.hint: reversibility of actions irreversible consequences
topics.default_q: If a wrong result or recommendation is noticed, can it be corrected?

topics.title: Reach
topics.hint: scale reach number of persons affected speed
topics.default_q: How many people could be affected by such a mistake?

topics.title: Personal data
topics.hint: data and data governance personal data special categories
topics.default_q: What type of personal data does the agent work with?
options: Ordinary personal data (such as name, contact details, order history)
Sensitive data too (such as health, religion, ethnic origin)

topics.title: Vulnerable groups
topics.hint: vulnerable groups children elderly persons with disabilities adverse impact
topics.default_q: Can vulnerable groups such as children, elderly or disabled people be affected by the agent's decisions?

topics.title: Direct interaction with people
topics.hint: AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons informed they are interacting with an AI system
topics.default_q: Does the agent communicate directly with people, for example by chat, e-mail or voice? This includes your own staff as well as customers or suppliers.

topics.title: Content generation
topics.hint: synthetic audio image video or text content marked machine-readable format
topics.default_q: Does the agent write free-form text, or produce audio, images or video, as its output? Filling in structured fields or taking actions (for example placing an order) does not count.
options: No, it only takes actions or fills in structured fields
Yes, free-form text (for example e-mails or summaries)

topics.title: Content resembling a real person/event
topics.hint: deep fake disclose artificially generated or manipulated text published to inform the public
topics.default_q: Is that output published, or does it imitate real people, places or events? Please pick the closest description.
options: No: nothing is published and nothing imitates real people, places or events
It imitates real people, places or events (for example a realistic voice, image or video)
It writes text that is published to inform the public about matters of public interest
Neither, but it is sent to outside parties (for example customers or suppliers)

topics.title: Responsible owner
topics.hint: accountability responsible owner roles AI literacy
topics.default_q: Is there a named person who is the responsible owner of this system?

topics.title: Written risk/impact assessment
topics.hint: risk management system impact assessment documented
topics.default_q: Has a written risk assessment been done for this use?

topics.title: Logging
topics.hint: logging trajectory logs record-keeping traceability
topics.default_q: Are the agent's actions and recommendations recorded so that they can be traced later?

topics.title: Monitoring and incident handling
topics.hint: post-deployment monitoring incident response reporting
topics.default_q: Is there someone who monitors the agent's live behaviour and is there an incident process?

topics.title: Documentation
topics.hint: technical documentation instructions for use data provenance
topics.default_q: Is there a current document that explains how the agent works and what its limits are?

topics.title: External content and memory
topics.hint: prompt injection indirect instructions untrusted content memory poisoning
topics.default_q: Does the agent read external content such as web pages, e-mails or documents; if so, is there a safeguard so that this content cannot steer the agent?
options: It does not read external content

topics.title: Loop and budget limit
topics.hint: stop conditions iteration budget caps loops cascading failure
topics.default_q: Is there a step, time or budget limit so that the agent cannot run in an endless loop?

topics.title: Supplier and change control
topics.hint: third-party suppliers change control reassessment after changes
topics.default_q: Does the system use a third-party model or tool?
options: Yes, but there is no process

topics.title: Conformity activities
topics.hint: conformity assessment registration quality management system
topics.default_q: Has your organisation planned the formal checks and registration that the law requires for a high-risk use of AI?

topics.title: User information
topics.hint: transparency obligations inform persons interacting with an AI system synthetic content disclosure
topics.default_q: Do users know that they are interacting with AI, or that content was generated by AI (for example, is it stated on screen)?

topics.title: Criteria of the score
topics.hint: evaluation or classification of natural persons social behaviour personal characteristics criminal offence risk assessment profiling
topics.default_q: Which criteria and data is the score or evaluation calculated from?
topics.simple_q: Does this evaluation also include data such as social media, general behaviour or personality analysis, or a prediction of crime/fraud risk?
simple_options: Yes, social behaviour or personality data is used
Yes, crime or fraud risk is assessed

topics.title: Safeguards during and after execution
topics.hint: human oversight intervene stop monitoring reversal
topics.default_q: Which of these safeguards exist for what the agent does? Tick everything that applies. (Approval before an action is a separate topic and is not covered here.)
topics.simple_q: In short: can a person stop the agent at once, watch it while it runs, review what it did afterwards, and undo a wrong action? Tick what applies, or say you are not sure.

items.label: A person can pause or stop it immediately
A person can watch what it does while it is running
A person reviews what it did afterwards
A wrong action can be reversed or cancelled afterwards

multi.unsure_label: I'm not sure about some of these

topics.title: Delegation and approval boundaries
topics.hint: delegation permissions authority approval boundary
topics.default_q: Do either of these apply to the agent? Tick what applies, or choose “None of these”.
topics.simple_q: In short: does the agent hand work to other agents or tools, and can any privileged or administrative route skip the approval step? Tick what applies, or say you are not sure.

items.label: It can hand work to other agents or automated tools
Some privileged or administrative routes can skip the approval step

multi.unsure_label: I'm not sure about some of these

topics.title: Aggregate limits
topics.hint: aggregate limits cumulative cap transactions
topics.default_q: Besides the limit on each single action (for example each order or payment), is there a total cap, such as per day, per week or per recipient, so that many small actions cannot add up beyond it?
options: Yes, there is a total cap
No, only each single action is limited

topics.title: Ability to stop
topics.hint: stop kill switch halt intervention human oversight
topics.default_q: If a mistake is noticed, can someone stop the agent immediately?

topics.title: Ability to roll back
topics.hint: rollback recovery reversibility of actions incident
topics.default_q: If an action taken by the agent is wrong, can it be undone?

topics.title: Human re-examination
topics.hint: human oversight review of outputs contestability affected persons ability to override
topics.default_q: Can a human re-examine the file of a person adversely affected by the agent's result (for example a rejected application or request)?

topics.title: Type of task
topics.hint: not high-risk narrow procedural task preparatory task improve result of previously completed human activity detect decision-making patterns
topics.default_q: Which of these is closest to the agent's task?
options: A narrow procedural step (e.g. a format check)
Improving the result of a task a human already completed
Detecting decision patterns (without replacing human assessment)
Preparation for an assessment a human will make
topics.simple_q: For example: does the agent only tidy or summarise a form, or does it produce an assessment or score about a person?

topics.title: Steering the decision
topics.hint: does not materially influence the outcome of decision making
topics.default_q: Does the agent's output in practice steer the decision a human makes?
topics.simple_q: For example: does the decision maker mostly apply the agent's recommendation as it is?

With methods the user will not be aware of

slot_desc.purpose: the single intended purpose/task of the agent
slot_desc.affected_decisions: people and decisions affected by its output
slot_desc.eu_link: use in the EU, or output affecting people/organisations in the EU
slot_desc.org_role: whether the organisation developed the agent or only uses it
slot_desc.g_biometric: whether it processes biometric data such as face, voice or fingerprints
slot_desc.g_influence: whether the agent's PURPOSE is to steer the people it meets towards a specific behaviour (buying, voting, giving up, ...); recommending to a decision maker or influencing a decision is NOT this
slot_desc.g_person_eval: whether the agent assigns people a score, rank or risk/suitability value (only this fact; it does NOT by itself mean social scoring or crime prediction)
slot_desc.annex3_area: sensitive use area (recruitment/HR->employment, credit/insurance/essential services->essential_services, education, law enforcement, migration, justice, critical infrastructure) or none; FILL IN if the user states the area explicitly (e.g. 'recruitment agent'); biometrics is asked separately via g_biometric
slot_desc.annex1_product: whether the agent is a safety component of a product (medical device, machinery, ...)
slot_desc.art6_3_exception: whether it only does a narrow procedural task / improves a completed human task / detects decision patterns / a preparatory task
slot_desc.influences_decision: whether its output in practice steers a human decision
slot_desc.t_interacts_people: whether the agent talks/messages DIRECTLY with a person (customer, employee, ...)
slot_desc.t_synthetic_content: whether it generates and publishes audio/image/video/text content
slot_desc.t_deepfake_public_text: content that looks like a real person/event, or text published to inform the public
slot_desc.personal_data: type of personal data the agent uses
slot_desc.vulnerable_groups: whether vulnerable groups (children, elderly, ...) are affected
slot_desc.action_mode: the agent's authority (see the explanation below)
slot_desc.human_review: whether the decision maker can see the basis of a recommendation/draft and object before deciding (not a review of actions afterwards: that is post_action_review)
slot_desc.approval_bound: (if approval exists) whether the approval is specific to that single action
slot_desc.limits_enforced: whether limits are technical or only instructions
slot_desc.authority_expansion: whether it can expand its own authority/access
slot_desc.delegates_to_agents: whether it delegates work to other agents/tools
slot_desc.max_harm: worst reasonable harm if it fails
slot_desc.reversibility: whether the harm can be reversed
slot_desc.eval_uses_social_traits: whether the score/evaluation also uses data on a person's social behaviour, personality traits or general online behaviour (only if the user said so)
slot_desc.eval_predicts_crime: whether the evaluation also predicts the likelihood of a person committing a crime/fraud (only if the user said so)
slot_desc.approval_exists: whether a human approval is obtained before an action is taken
slot_desc.can_stop: whether someone can stop the agent immediately
slot_desc.can_rollback: whether an action taken by the agent can be undone if it is wrong
slot_desc.human_reexam: whether a human can re-examine the file of a person adversely affected by the agent's result
slot_desc.monitoring_live: whether a person can watch what the agent does while it is running (monitoring during execution; not approval before execution)
slot_desc.post_action_review: whether a person reviews what the agent did afterwards (post-action review; not approval before execution)
slot_desc.aggregate_limit: whether a total cap (per day, week or supplier) limits the sum of the agent's actions, not only each single action
slot_desc.approval_bypass: whether privileged or administrative paths can skip the approval step
slot_desc.wf_threshold: derived: a workflow with an amount or limit threshold was declared
slot_desc.annex1_third_party: whether that product needs a third-party (notified body) conformity assessment

slot_help.action_mode: info_only=only produces information; recommend=gives recommendations, a human decides and acts; draft=prepares drafts, a human sends/executes; approved_action=acts only after human approval specific to that action; envelope_action=acts within defined limits without approval for each action; self_expanding=can expand or delegate its own scope or authority
slot_help.p_*: none=the user explicitly said it does not apply; possible=may apply/unclear; supported=the necessary conditions of the prohibition are supported by the answers AND exception/scope/date were considered and no exception applies; excepted=an exception applies; unknown=don't know (p_* values are normally derived from the g_* gate answers; fill them in only if a detail question was asked)
